messages:
kai: ran into duplicate webhook calls from the onboarding sample when a streaming request hit 429 during token refresh. customers confused. proposing a small, consistent SDK primitive to reduce surprises.

tara: yep. stream resumes are the tricky part. what's the primitive?

kai: add `safeReplay` opt-in in SDKs. it does three small things: attach Idempotency-Key for unary ops, keep a last-resume token for streams, and coalesce parallel retries (singleflight). default off.

ben: how heavyweight is this? we want parity but no huge API surface.

kai: only one boolean and an optional backoff config. defaults are conservative so most users never touch them. example defaults: max_retries=5, base_ms=200, max_ms=4000, jitter=full. retry_on: 429/503/network_error.

tara: server-side: how do we avoid storing tokens forever?

kai: server keeps resume log per request for a short TTL (default 60s). Dedicated/private customers can raise it per-route; hosted keeps safe default.

ben: need singleflight around token refresh or we'll still see double replays.

kai: agreed. SDK should coalesce refresh so only one refresh + resume happens for a logical request id.

ci-bot: created ticket DEVEX-913: add e2e that simulates 429 + token rotation during streaming and validate safeReplay behavior. assigned to @ben.

tara: also add SDK hooks for observability: onReplayAttempt, onReplayResult(replayed|fast-forwarded|skipped). Console will show those traces so support can debug.

kai: adding a tiny sample app patch: express webhook that dedupes on Idempotency-Key + stream producer demonstrating resume. will open PR tonight.

ben: sounds reasonable. make sure docs explain tradeoffs: reduces duplicates but adds small resume latency.

tara: thumbs up. parity owners for node/python/go please review when PRs land.

kai: thanks all.
